source.title: An Empirical Study of Data Scale, Model Complexity, and Input Modalities in Visual Generalization

record.tranche_reason: Compares fully connected and convolutional architectures on image classification using test accuracy, bearing on V3, but does not reproduce the original studies’ settings or methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own architecture-comparison results for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as rows. Results on data scale, input modalities, and polynomial fitting do not directly test the mapped versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out image-classification accuracy of fully connected and convolutional networks trained from scratch with gradient methods on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, testing V3 with the same basic method and measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors also conclude that grayscale reduces accuracy and that added gradient, edge, and wavelet features benefit MLPs more consistently than ResNets, suggesting that alignment between architecture and input structure matters. They present architectural mechanisms as hypotheses requiring ablations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, MLP/AlexNet/ResNet comparisons, and test Top-1 accuracy; it does not reproduce V3’s named datasets, comparisons, or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that test performance changes with dataset, training-set size, architecture, and input modality. For the architecture comparison in V3, it reports worse MLP accuracy than convolutional-model accuracy on both CIFAR datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing ResNet depth and parameter count does not consistently improve test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benefits from increasing network depth depend on data scale and task difficulty under this fixed training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Polynomial test error varies nonmonotonically with degree and depends strongly on sample size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polynomial complexity and sample size interact in this noisy function-fitting task; this does not establish post-interpolation neural-network width behavior.

record.problems: The main experiments use a single random seed and report no mean or variance across repeated runs. There is no separate validation set; Table 2 and Table 3 select the epoch with the best test accuracy. No data augmentation, weight decay, Dropout, or learning-rate scheduling is used. The architecture comparison does not isolate local connectivity as the cause of the performance difference.
record.rows_left_out: Rows on training-set-size sweeps and input modalities were left out because those conditions do not test the mapped versions. Polynomial fitting results were also left out because the authors state that this preliminary task is not direct evidence about deep networks.

untested.parts: No fixed-random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No network-width sweep through and beyond an established zero-training-error threshold; comparisons of ResNet depth and polynomial degree do not test this version.
Does not isolate local connectivity, train fully connected networks to learn sparse local connections, or initialize them from trained convolutional networks.
No optimizer comparison; all main experiments use Adam.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch recipe adaptation.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving augmentation and removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization measures.
No memorization-based identification and removal of examples.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded accuracy values match Tables 2–3. Results use a single seed and select the best epoch on the test set, without a separate validation set or repeated-run uncertainty. The architecture comparison does not isolate local connectivity. Contrary to the record's recipe description, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 are named V3 settings. The smaller-training-set and input-modality comparisons also bear on V3: convolutional accuracy exceeds MLP accuracy throughout those tables. These omissions are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare random-label and natural-label generalization.
Does not sweep one-hidden-layer ReLU width past the zero-training-error threshold on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Does not isolate local connectivity as the cause of the architecture gap, test learned sparse local connections, or initialize a fully connected network from a trained convolutional one.
Uses Adam only; no optimizer comparison or broader optimizer tuning.
Uses batch size 128 only; no batch-size comparison or adapted large-batch recipe.
Does not compare dropout settings or test the interaction with data augmentation; explicit regularization is not used.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization measures.
Does not identify or remove memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, 50000 training images; Adam for 100 epochs without augmentation, weight decay, or dropout
relationships.reason: R1–R7 show convolutional accuracies of 76.54–87.09%, exceeding the MLP's 54.70%.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher convolutional accuracy under Adam remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100, 50000 training images; Adam for 100 epochs without augmentation, weight decay, or dropout
relationships.reason: R8–R14 show convolutional accuracies of 43.24–60.03%, exceeding the MLP's 26.45%.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher convolutional accuracy under Adam remains unverified.
